items.entity: Beam design domain (box size and proportions)
items.description: Sec. 5.4 says only 'Given a design domain as illustrated in Figure 9(a)'. No dimensions are stated for the optimization domain. The only numbers are the printed-specimen size, 120×48×48 mm^3 (second paragraph of Sec. 5.4). This is probably the design domain, but the text never says so. That the 120 mm axis is the span is implied, not stated.
readings: 120 × 48 × 48 (length × width × height, L:W:H = 2.5:1:1), assumed identical to the printed specimens
Normalized box 2.5 × 1 × 1 (same proportions, different absolute size)

items.entity: Supports on the beam bottom ('bottom sides')
items.description: Fig. 9 caption: 'The bottom sides are fixed.' The text does not say whether the supports are lines along the two bottom end edges, strips of finite length on the bottom face near each end, or positions set in from the ends to match the rig's support span (the span is never given). It also does not say whether they cover the full 48 mm width. The exact geometry appears only in Fig. 9(a).
readings: Full-width line supports along the bottom edges at both ends (x = 0 and x = L, z = 0)
Full-width strips on the bottom face at each end (e.g., x in [0, 0.05L] and [0.95L, L])
Full-width line supports set in from the ends to mimic the test-rig span (e.g., at x = 0.1L and x = 0.9L)

items.description: The Fig. 9 caption calls the bottom sides 'fixed', but Sec. 5.4 describes a three-point bending test, which normally uses simple (roller) supports. The text does not say which displacement components are constrained.
readings: Clamped: u_x = u_y = u_z = 0 on both support regions
Simply supported: only u_z = 0 on both supports, plus the minimum extra constraints needed to stop rigid-body motion
Pin-roller: all components fixed at one end; only the vertical (and lateral) component fixed at the other

items.entity: Mid-span load on the beam top
items.description: Fig. 9 caption: 'the force is uniformly applied at the center of the beam top'. The text does not give the size or shape of the loaded zone (a line across the width, a strip of finite width, or a central patch) or how far it extends across the width. Only Fig. 9(a) shows it.
readings: Line load spread uniformly across the full width at mid-span on the top face (x = L/2, z = H)
Uniform pressure on a full-width strip centred at mid-span (width about 0.05L to 0.1L)
Uniform pressure on a small central patch of the top face (about 0.2W × 0.2W, centred at x = L/2, y = W/2)

items.entity: Mid-span load on the beam top
items.description: No force or pressure value is given for the optimization (Sec. 5.4, Fig. 9 caption). Fig. 10(b) shows only the experimental force-displacement curves.
readings: Total force F = 1 (normalized)
Unit traction (pressure = 1) over the loaded area
A physical test-level total force (e.g., 1000 N)

items.entity: Base-material Young's modulus (tensor C* in Sec. 4.3)
items.description: Sec. 4.3 introduces the base-material elastic tensor C*, but its values are never given. Sec. 5.4 does not name the additive-manufacturing material either.
readings: E = 1 (normalized)
E ≈ 2.5 GPa (typical photopolymer resin)
E ≈ 1.7 GPa (typical SLS PA12)

items.description: The base material's Poisson's ratio, which enters C* and therefore the homogenized tensor C^H, is not stated anywhere.

items.entity: Stiffness-density (homogenized) law for the porous units of Table 2(a) and 2(c)
items.description: The optimization uses C^H(rho) fitted with Eq. (26), c_ij(rho)/c_ij* = a1*exp(a2*rho) - a1. The values of a1 and a2 (for each coefficient and each unit) are never given. Fig. 4(b) shows fitted curves only as a graph, and only for an unidentified 'symmetric porous unit'. The tensors are anisotropic (9 constants), and how the unit axes line up with the beam axes is implicit. A single-material isotropic solver must substitute its own interpolation law, and that choice changes the graded density layout. The two units are separate runs (results in Fig. 9(b) and 9(c)).
readings: The paper's exponential law with unit-specific fitted a1, a2 for each of the 9 orthotropic constants (values unknown)
Isotropic SIMP proxy E(rho) = rho^3 E0
Isotropic Gibson-Ashby-type power law E(rho) = rho^2 E0 (bending-dominated)
Linear law E(rho) = rho E0 (no penalization)

items.entity: Symmetry class of the natural-sample unit (Table 2(a))
items.description: Sec. 5.4 calls both units 'symmetric'. Elsewhere, units made from natural samples are fitted with symmetric degree r = 1, i.e. periodic but not symmetric: Sec. 4.1, the Fig. 1 caption ('periodic implicit unit' for the natural sample), and Sec. 5.7. This decides whether C^H is orthotropic (9 constants, as in Sec. 4.3) or fully anisotropic.
readings: Symmetric unit (r = floor(n/2) in each direction): orthotropic C^H with 9 independent constants
Periodic-only unit (r = 1): fully anisotropic C^H (up to 21 constants, with shear-normal coupling)

items.description: Eq. (27) bounds the B-spline density coefficients by rho_min <= rho_ijk <= rho_max (the minimum and maximum relative density of the porous units). No values are given for Sec. 5.4.
readings: rho_min = 0.001, rho_max = 1.0 (standard SIMP)
rho_min = 0.1, rho_max = 0.9
rho_min = 0.2, rho_max = 0.8

items.description: Sec. 4.3: the density is a B-spline field with N_u×N_v×N_w control coefficients rho_ijk; the spline degree is not stated either. This control net is the only smoothing; no filter is mentioned. Neither the net size nor the degree is given for the beam, so the matching filter radius for an element-based structured-grid solver cannot be determined.
readings: Cubic B-spline density with one coefficient per unit cell (e.g., 10 × 4 × 4)
Cubic B-spline density with a finer net (e.g., 20 × 8 × 8)
Element-wise densities with a density filter of radius 1.5 elements
Element-wise densities with a filter radius of about one unit-cell size (e.g., 12 mm)

items.entity: Analysis discretization of the beam (IGA / finite elements)
items.description: Sec. 4.3 analyses the beam with isogeometric analysis (IGA) on a B-spline solid, but the number of elements N_e, the basis degree and the refinement are not reported. A structured-grid resolution must therefore be chosen.
readings: 30 × 12 × 12 hexahedral elements (4 mm)
60 × 24 × 24 elements (2 mm)
120 × 48 × 48 elements (1 mm)

items.entity: Optimality Criteria update and stopping rule
items.description: Sec. 4.3 says Optimality Criteria (OC) is used, but gives no move limit, damping exponent, convergence tolerance or iteration limit.
readings: move = 0.2, eta = 0.5, stop when the maximum density change < 0.01
move = 0.1, eta = 0.5, fixed 100 to 200 iterations
move = 0.05, stop when the relative compliance change < 1e-3

items.entity: Number of porous unit cells E_u × E_v × E_w in the beam
items.description: Sec. 2.2 builds the structure from E_u×E_v×E_w units, but the counts (and so the unit-cell size) for the 120×48×48 mm beam are not stated. They do not enter the homogenized optimization directly, but they may set the scale of the density net or filter, and they define the final porous model.
readings: 5 × 2 × 2 cells (24 mm)
10 × 4 × 4 cells (12 mm)
20 × 8 × 8 cells (6 mm)

items.description: The Sec. 5.4 text says the design domain is in Fig. 9(a) and also that the optimized density fields are in 'Figure 9(a) and Figure 9(c)'. The caption instead puts the design domain and boundary conditions in 9(a), and the optimized fields in 9(b) (Table 2(a) unit) and 9(c) (Table 2(c) unit). This does not change the problem setup, but it confuses which panel defines the boundary conditions.
readings: Caption version: 9(a) = domain and boundary conditions, 9(b) = Table 2(a) result, 9(c) = Table 2(c) result
Text version: optimized fields in 9(a) and 9(c)
